# Results — Study 443 (Volume Profile POC)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim — **price
returns to the volume-profile Point of Control (POC), the level with the most traded volume,
like a magnet** — tested on a 6-name liquid basket of yfinance **5-minute** bars. For each
session we build a volume profile (50 price bins, typical-price volume), take the POC, stamp it
onto the next session, and ask: did the next day's range touch the prior POC **more often than a
distance-matched random control level** (same gap from the open, random side)? Then we fade the
open toward the POC and charge a spread. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance **5-minute** RTH bars (auto-adjusted) — SPY, QQQ, AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, TSLA (public, no key) |
| Window | 2026-03-31 → **2026-06-23** (~60 trading days; Yahoo's 5m cap is ~60 calendar days) |
| As-of | **2026-06-23** (last *complete* session; the in-progress current day is dropped) |
| Sessions / events | **348** session rows; **336** events with the open ≥ 5 bps from the prior POC |
| Fingerprint | `10ce6e8c7ecb` (sha1[:12] of the `open_gap` column) |
| POC / touch / costs | 50-bin typical-price volume profile; touch = day range straddles the prior POC (tol sweep 0–20 bps); fade charged **1 bp** one-way × 2 legs |

> **Short-span & capacity caveat (loud).** Yahoo serves only ~60 trading days of 5-minute bars,
> so this is a **short tape** — 336 events on 6 liquid names. That is plenty to *reject* a strong
> magnet on liquid equities, but **not** enough to certify a tiny conditional edge (for that you
> want years of ES/NQ futures tick data). And the subject is **intraday levels**, where the
> bid-ask spread, paid on entry and exit of every fade, is the binding constraint — intraday
> levels die to the spread. Survivorship is *not* an issue here: this is a within-name,
> day-over-day level test, not a cross-sectional surviving-names basket.

## The signal — POC touch-rate vs a distance-matched random control

The honest estimand is the **difference** of touch-rates, POC minus a random level the *same
distance* from the open (a volatile range touches *any* nearby level often). The *t* is a paired
one-sample *t* of the per-event (POC-touch − control-touch) indicator; the HAC *t* is Newey-West
(5 lags) for the day-over-day autocorrelation of touch outcomes.

| metric | POC | random control | edge (POC − ctrl) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| touch-rate | **49.7%** | **53.3%** | **−3.6 pp** |
| 95% Wilson interval | [44.4, 55.0] | [47.9, 58.5] | — |
| paired *t* | | | **−1.28** |
| **HAC *t*** | | | **−1.32** |

The POC is touched **less** than a distance-matched random level, and the difference is
statistically indistinguishable from zero (HAC *t* = −1.32, the wrong sign, far from the **t ≥ 2**
bar). The "magnet" is an artefact of volatile intraday ranges touching nearby levels — the POC
is not special. A **shuffle-the-POC placebo** (re-pair each session's range with a permuted POC
offset, 5,000 draws) puts the true POC touch-rate **inside the luck cloud**: **p = 0.682** (the
true pairing is touched no more than a random pairing).

## The trade — fade the open toward the POC

Short above the POC / long below, target the level (book the open→POC gap if touched, else
open→close). **1 bp** one-way × 2 legs — generous for these names.

| | value |
|---|--:|
| trades | 336 |
| target-hit rate | 49.7% |
| **gross** mean per-trade | **−0.102%** (t = −1.46) |
| **net** mean per-trade (1 bp/leg) | **−0.122%** (t = −1.75) |
| break-even one-way cost | **−5.1 bps** |

The fade is **gross-negative** — it loses money *before* any spread, so the break-even cost is
**negative**: there is no edge to pay even a zero spread out of. Intraday spreads only dig deeper.

## Robustness — touch-tolerance sweep

A touch counts if the range comes within `tol × price` of the level (same for POC and control).

| tolerance | POC | control | edge | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0 bps  | 49.7% | 53.3% | **−3.6 pp** | −1.32 |
| 5 bps  | 52.1% | 54.8% | −2.7 pp | −1.04 |
| 10 bps | 54.2% | 57.1% | −3.0 pp | −1.14 |
| 20 bps | 58.3% | 61.6% | −3.3 pp | −1.26 |

Loosening the touch rule lifts **both** rates together; the edge stays **negative at every
tolerance**. There is no definition of "touch" under which the POC beats a coin-flip level.

No name shows a magnet; the one large value (TSLA) is **negative**. Per-name samples are ~55 days
— the pooled estimate is the headline; the cross-section just confirms the absence of any positive
signal.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

On a deterministic panel where we **plant** a pull toward the POC (an OU-like reversion of the
close to the level), the detector behaves exactly as it must:

| planted pull | POC | control | edge | HAC *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.0** (no magnet) | 49.3% | 48.7% | +0.6 pp | **+0.44** | 0.011 |
| **+0.7** (strong magnet) | 76.5% | 61.0% | **+15.5 pp** | **+7.49** | 0.000 |

With **no** planted pull the detector sits at HAC *t* ≈ 0 (it does not manufacture a magnet from
noise); a strong planted pull lights up at HAC *t* = 7.49. The harness is unbiased and *can*
detect a real magnet — so the flat/negative real-tape result is a genuine **absence**, not a
broken detector.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The POC is touched **49.7%** of the time vs **53.3%** for a distance-matched
  random level (edge **−3.6 pp**, HAC **t = −1.32**, shuffle-POC placebo **p = 0.68**) — the wrong
  sign and nowhere near the desk's **t ≥ 2** bar, robust to touch tolerance and present in no name.
  The "magnet" is volatile intraday range touching nearby levels, not any pull from the POC.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Fading the open toward the POC is **gross-negative** (−0.102% per
  trade, t = −1.46); the break-even one-way cost is **−5.1 bps** — no edge to pay any spread out
  of, and intraday spreads are exactly where levels die.
- **"Price returns to the POC"? — BUSTED.** The POC is touched *no more* (a touch less) than a
  random level the same distance from the open, at every tolerance. The claim mistakes a feature
  of a volatile tape for a force. (Short span ~60 trading days, named loudly — enough to reject
  the headline magnet on liquid names, not to chase a tiny edge on years of futures tick data.)
